headline: Equity surge caps the rally: 10Y CCDC edges to a 1-year low of 1.608% while TL futures stall
summary: CGBs rallied in the morning on easier funding and PBOC bond buying, then gave back part of it as stocks surged after lunch. The CCDC 10-year fell 1.3bp to 1.608%, another 1-year low, and the 30-year 0.9bp to 2.042%, while the 2-year and 7-year led (both −1.2bp) and the 5-year lagged (−0.5bp to 1.325%). Policy banks were mixed: CDB 1–3Y fell about 3bp and CDB 10-year 1.2bp to 1.646%, 3.8bp over CGB, but ADBC and EXIM 10-year fell only 0.7bp, widening to 7.4bp and 6.5bp over CGB.
drivers: Stocks rip higher and cap the long end

The Shanghai Composite jumped 2.16%, ChiNext 6.4% and the STAR 50 9.9% on turnover of about RMB2.05tn, after the PBOC's buyback relending rate cut to 1% took effect with over RMB200bn of bank applications and national-team ETFs drew near-record inflows. The long end gave back its morning gains: TL settled 0.03% lower while T rose 0.08% and TF 0.05%.

The PBOC's disclosure that its net CGB purchases increased again in October lifted bonds early, and the active 10-year traded at 1.60% before the equity rally. It signals the central bank is still adding duration demand, which limits how far yields can back up.
Funding keeps easing under the overnight anchor

The PBOC ran RMB257.5bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB772bn maturing, a RMB514.5bn net drain, yet overnight Shibor fell 2.4bp to 1.265%, 7-day 1.3bp to 1.329% and 14-day to its lowest since May. That helped the 2-year and 1–3Y policy banks, where CDB 1Y and 3Y fell about 3bp.
Soft services PMI and firm policy bank demand

The RatingDog services PMI fell to 50.8 (forecast 51.5, prior 51.6) with selling prices cut again, keeping the low-inflation case intact. ADBC sold 5-year and 10-year bonds at 1.4031% and 1.6379%, below CCDC valuations, with 7.0x and 6.5x cover; Huafa-linked bonds stayed volatile but did not hit rates.
data: Oct RatingDog services PMI (Nov 4)
50.8 (f 51.5, p 51.6); composite 52.0 (p 52.4); selling prices cut for a 2nd month
Slowest services growth since July with falling prices supports low yields, though bonds sold off later on equities.
Oct RatingDog mfg PMI (Nov 2)
52.0 (f 51.6, p 52.1); output fastest since April; 11th month of expansion
Private and export-facing firms are holding up, which tempers the weak official print but did not stop the bond rally.
Oct official PMIs (Oct 31)
Mfg 49.3 (f 50.0, p 50.1); new orders 49.4; non-mfg 49.7 (p 50.2); composite 49.7
Back in contraction with softer prices, which supports low yields and the case for continued easy funding.
Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
view: Neutral leaning long for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.58–1.64% CCDC range. Funding is easing under the 1.25% overnight anchor, the PBOC is still buying CGBs and services data are soft, so the trend still points lower, but the 10Y long hit its 1.61% target and was closed, fund duration is near record highs and a state-backed equity rebound can trigger quick profit-taking around 1.60%. I would re-buy the 10-year only on a back-up to 1.635–1.64%, keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch, stay underweight policy banks against CGBs at 10Y and the long end, and prefer ADBC/EXIM over CDB. A lasting equity rally or a new credit or redemption scare would take the 10-year back to 1.65%, while weak October trade, inflation or credit data could push it through 1.60%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 1.2bp to 1.216%, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average 1.309%), and the 1-year 0.4bp to 1.166% as overnight Shibor slid to 1.265%. Easier funding is pulling the front end down, but with the policy rate at 1.25% there is little room left unless the corridor moves.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if the overnight rate is cut below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 5-year lagged, down only 0.5bp to 1.325%, so 2s5s10s rose 1.5bp to −17.2bp, still in the 4th percentile against a −7.6bp average; 5s7s10s is −9.5bp (0th percentile) after the 7-year fell 1.2bp to 1.419%. The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is at 28.2bp (67th percentile, average 26.4bp), 0.8bp in the money and inside the 31bp stop.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: Target hit: the long from 1.65% reached 1.61% as the 10-year fell to 1.608%, a 4.2bp gain, so it is closed. The outright yield is at a 1-year low, but against neighbours it still screens cheap: 7s10s20s is −24.1bp, in the 84th percentile against a −29.3bp average.
buckets.call: Profit taken at 1.61%; re-buy 10-year CGBs at 1.635–1.64%, target 1.60%, stop 1.665%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year fell 0.9bp to 2.042%, at its 1-year low, and 10s30s rose 0.4bp to 43.4bp, in the 30th percentile against a 45.6bp average. TL futures were flat as stocks rallied, and 30s50s at 12.4bp (8th percentile) leaves the ultra-long block little cushion ahead of Nov–Dec supply.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.8bp over CGB, in the 4th percentile against a 9.9bp average, and the CDB 5-year spread 9.6bp (2nd percentile); the CDB 2-year spread is 13.6bp (5th percentile). The switch from ~3bp is open and 0.8bp in the money; strong ADBC auctions show demand is still firm, so the widening is slow.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 3.6bp more than CDB, up 0.5bp on the day and in the 80th percentile against a 1.3bp average; EXIM is 2.7bp over (68th percentile, average 2.0bp). ADBC's new 10-year cleared at 1.6379% with 6.5x cover, well below the 1.682% curve, so the pickup is about supply and liquidity, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 4.9bp over CGB, at its 1-year low (1st percentile, average 10.6bp), and the 30-year 11.0bp, also a 1-year low (average 12.7bp). Policy bank long bonds again moved one for one with CGBs, so the spread offers no cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

watch: Next: US payrolls (Nov 6), October trade and FX reserves (around Nov 7), October CPI/PPI and credit data the following week, daily PBOC overnight operations at 1.25%, front-loaded November local bond supply, the FX RRR hike taking effect on Nov 15, and October activity data in mid-November.
sources: Reuters via Yahoo Finance (services PMI, Nov 4)
